title: Joni Ernst addresses veterans' contributions and comments on government shutdown negotiations
text:
Sen. Joni Ernst, US Senator for Iowa | Joni Ernst Official Webste
Sen. Joni Ernst, US Senator for Iowa | Joni Ernst Official Webste
Senator Joni Ernst, a Republican representing Iowa, posted several statements on her X (formerly Twitter) account addressing both Veterans Day and the recent government shutdown debate.
On November 11, 2025, Ernst wrote: "America owes everything we have to those who served. Thank a veteran today."
The following day, on November 12, 2025, she commented on the ongoing government shutdown negotiations in Washington: "Democrats claimed the suffering of Americans was 'leverage' throughout the failed Schumer Shutdown. It never should have happened." Later that same day, Ernst urged prompt legislative action to address the consequences of the shutdown: "The failed Schumer Shutdown is finally almost over. The House must act swiftly to get our servicemembers and air traffic controllers paid, restore SNAP and WIC, and get Washington back to serving the American people!"
Ernst's remarks come after a period of federal government funding lapses often referred to as "shutdowns," which can result in disruptions to public services such as pay delays for federal employees—including military personnel—and interruptions to assistance programs like SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) and WIC (Women, Infants, and Children). During these episodes, political leaders have debated responsibility for stalled negotiations. The term "Schumer Shutdown" references Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer’s role during recent funding disputes.
As an Army veteran herself and a member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, Senator Ernst has frequently advocated for military families and emphasized bipartisan solutions to avoid future funding gaps.
